prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1249; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling in the left lane of a two-lane road in Pasadena, Texas, when the front of the vehicle struck the front of a second vehicle operated by Driver 2, which had crossed into the same lane. The impact was low speed, and both vehicles came to rest at the point of contact. Driver 1 remained seated on arrival of the first responding unit and reported pain in the lower back. A Passenger was also present in the vehicle and was seen and accounted for at the scene. Driver 2 stated that the collision occurred as Driver 1 described, and two independent witnesses gave the same account. Photographs taken at the scene show front-end damage to both vehicles that is consistent with the reported impact. Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the policy covering the vehicle. Officers found no indication of prior damage to the vehicle. The reported back complaint is consistent with the kind and force of a frontal impact of this nature. No citations were issued at the scene.
